facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
presented to the emergency department with a headache for 2 weeks
vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
Right-sided headache 1 week later and right vision loss 2 days prior to presentation

support_spans: Serum IgG4: 277 mg/dL (normal, <123 mg/dL)
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive
concepts.why: Elevated serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG4-positive plasma cells support the diagnosis of IgG4-related disease.

support_spans: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone, with extension of inflammation into the apex
Right eye visual acuity was limited to hand-motion detection
concepts.why: Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone and decreased visual acuity are consistent with orbital apex syndrome.

support_spans: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
contradict_spans: A man in his 70s with no history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
concepts.why: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation suggests chronic rhinosinusitis, but the patient's lack of history of chronic rhinosinusitis makes this diagnosis less likely.

support_spans: Sinus Cultures: Positive for Streptococcus constellatus
concepts.why: Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus support the diagnosis of streptococcal orbital cellulitis.

support_spans: Three weeks prior, he had rhinorrhea and was diagnosed with COVID-19
concepts.why: The patient's recent diagnosis with COVID-19 and subsequent development of symptoms suggest post-COVID-19 complications.
